questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has flashing lights and its signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must stop and stay stopped until the signal arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Reduced visibility at night makes it hard to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing with a guide dog or white cane. What should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield to a blind or partially blind pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has curves ahead.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians at intersections, with or without a crosswalk. Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn of trains. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers or ignore activated signals.

questions.question: What do yellow or red painted curbs mean?

options.text: Free parking areas.
Paid parking areas.
No parking zones.

questions.explanation: Red curbs mark fire lanes. Yellow curbs mark loading zones or other parking restrictions.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.explanation: Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not reduce alcohol from your body. Only time will lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.explanation: This warning sign is yellow with black markings. It tells drivers that a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be careful to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. All children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and concentrate on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.explanation: Stay calm and focus on driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Plan your travel time, drive at the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle breaks down?

options.text: Signal and pull into the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let them pass and get out of their way. Never compete with other drivers or try to challenge them.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take an alcohol test?

options.text: May lose your license.
Are exercising your right as a motorist.
Will face no negative consequences.

questions.explanation: If a police officer tells you to take an alcohol test, you must do it by law. You can lose your driver's license if you refuse.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Before starting your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Always buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs before you start driving.

questions.question: In Arkansas, must front seat passengers wear seat belts?

options.text: Optional.
Suggested.
Required by law.

questions.explanation: In Arkansas, front seat passengers must wear a seat belt by law. Wear your seat belt every time you drive, not just on long trips.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell you?

options.text: To speed up slightly.
That it is not safe to pass.
To maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass other vehicles in a "No passing zone." These signs are posted in areas where you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.question: Is it allowed to drive after taking medication that affects your driving?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
If you don't feel drowsy.
If it is prescribed by a physician.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of anything that impairs your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.
